# `.claude/hooks/code_docs.py`

<!-- generated by .claude/hooks/code_docs.py from .claude/hooks/code_docs.py (sha256 ae8458fba434ee8cabd65dbcc645619a861861262ba6af70781fcf73e194b5d8) on 2026-10-08; don't edit by hand, it's rewritten when the file changes -->

> Stop-hook worker that finds code files whose content changed and asks a headless Claude session to (re)write one Markdown doc per file under `docs/code/`, then rebuilds the docs index.

## What it does and why

Roman learns the project by reading one doc per code file. Writing those docs by hand would be slow and they would go stale. This script keeps them in sync: it hashes every code file, compares the hash with the one stored in the file's existing doc, and regenerates only the docs where the hash differs.

It is not a numbered BUILD_PLAN step. It is tooling, started by the Stop hook `document-code.sh` after each Claude turn.

Run it by hand from the repo root:

```
python3 .claude/hooks/code_docs.py
```

It uses only the standard library, but it needs the `claude` CLI on `PATH`, plus `git`.

## How it fits

```
Claude turn ends
   │  (Stop hook)
   ▼
document-code.sh ──► code_docs.py ──► git ls-files        (which files exist)
                          │       ──► .claude/agents/code-documenter.md  (instructions)
                          │       ──► private/CONTEXT.md (local only, optional: privacy rules)
                          │       ──► DECISIONS.md, learning/INDEX.md    (link targets)
                          │       ──► claude -p (headless Sonnet, no tools, no hooks)
                          ▼
                 docs/code/<path>.md   +   docs/code/README.md (index)
                 .claude/code-docs/{runs.log, lock, disabled}
```

- **Called by:** `document-code.sh` (see [document-code.sh.md](document-code.sh.md)), or by hand.
- **Reads:** the source files, `.claude/agents/code-documenter.md`, the privacy section of `private/CONTEXT.md` if that local-only file exists, `DECISIONS.md`, `learning/INDEX.md`, and the existing docs.
- **Writes:** `docs/code/**.md`, `docs/code/README.md`, `.claude/code-docs/runs.log`, and the lock file `.claude/code-docs/lock`.
- **Env vars:** `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` (the project root, set by Claude Code), and `DECISION_LOGGER_CHILD` (set to `1` for the child process so no hooks run again).
- **Off switch:** create the file `.claude/code-docs/disabled`.

## Walkthrough

### Lines 1–7: shebang and module docstring

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Stop-hook worker: (re)write docs/code/<path>.md for every code file whose content changed.
...
"""
```

- Line 1 is a shebang: when the file is run directly as a program, the OS starts `python3` to run it.
- The triple-quoted string at the top is the module docstring. It documents the file and is available as `__doc__`.
- It says the doc stores the sha256 of its source. This is the key idea: a file is documented again only when its content changes, no matter who changed it (Claude, Roman, or `git checkout`).

### Lines 18–25: constants

```python
PROJECT = Path(os.environ.get("CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
DOCS_DIR = PROJECT / "docs" / "code"
STATE_DIR = PROJECT / ".claude" / "code-docs"
AGENT_FILE = PROJECT / ".claude" / "agents" / "code-documenter.md"
CODE_EXTENSIONS = {".py", ".sh", ".sql", ".json", ".yaml", ".yml", ".toml", ".js", ".ts"}
SKIP_PREFIXES = ("docs/", "learning/")
MAX_SOURCE = 60_000  # characters of source sent to the model
HEADER = re.compile(r"<!-- generated by \.claude/hooks/code_docs\.py from (\S+) \(sha256 ([0-9a-f]{64})\)")
```

- `PROJECT`: the repo root. It uses `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` if set. Otherwise it takes this file's absolute path (`__file__`, resolved) and goes up two levels: `parents[0]` is `hooks`, `[1]` is `.claude`, `[2]` is the repo root.
- `DOCS_DIR`, `STATE_DIR`, `AGENT_FILE`: where the docs, the bookkeeping files, and the documenter's instructions live.
- `CODE_EXTENSIONS`: a set of file types that count as code. Sets give fast `in` checks.
- `SKIP_PREFIXES`: a tuple. `str.startswith` accepts a tuple, which is why it is used on line 39. Files under `docs/` (the generated docs) and `learning/` (the tutor's notes) are never documented. Without this, `.json` or `.md` files in those folders could trigger documentation of the output itself.
- `MAX_SOURCE`: caps the source at 60,000 characters. `60_000` is just a readable number.
- `HEADER`: a compiled regex that matches the comment this script writes into every doc. Group 1 is the source path (`\S+` is non-whitespace). Group 2 is exactly 64 hex characters, the sha256. The dots in the pattern are escaped (`\.`) so they match literal dots.

### Lines 28–31: `log_run`

```python
def log_run(msg: str) -> None:
    STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(STATE_DIR / "runs.log", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(f"{datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')} {msg}\n")
```

- Appends one timestamped line to `.claude/code-docs/runs.log`. A hook runs invisibly, so this log is the only way to see what happened.
- `mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` creates the folder and its parents, and does not fail if it already exists.
- `with open(..., "a")`: `with` closes the file automatically, even on an error. `"a"` means append.
- `isoformat(timespec='seconds')` gives e.g. `2026-10-08T14:05:09`.

### Lines 34–40: `code_files`

```python
def code_files() -> list[str]:
    """Tracked and untracked-but-not-ignored files (so .env and .venv never appear), filtered to code."""
    out = subprocess.run(["git", "ls-files", "--cached", "--others", "--exclude-standard"],
                         cwd=PROJECT, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    return sorted(p for p in out.splitlines()
                  if Path(p).suffix in CODE_EXTENSIONS and not p.startswith(SKIP_PREFIXES)
                  and (PROJECT / p).is_file())
```

- Asks git for the file list: `--cached` is tracked files, `--others` is untracked files, and `--exclude-standard` drops anything in `.gitignore`. That keeps `.env` and `.venv` out.
- `subprocess.run(...)`: `cwd` sets the folder, `capture_output=True` collects stdout/stderr, `text=True` gives strings instead of bytes, and `check=True` raises `CalledProcessError` if git fails (for example, outside a git repo). `.stdout` is the output text.
- The generator expression keeps a path only if its extension is in `CODE_EXTENSIONS`, it does not start with a skipped prefix, and it is a real file. The last check matters because `--cached` still lists files deleted from disk but not yet removed from git.
- `sorted(...)` returns a list in a stable order.

### Lines 43–46: `doc_path`

```python
def doc_path(src: str) -> Path:
    # ".claude/hooks/x.py" -> docs/code/_claude/hooks/x.py.md (hidden folders would hide the docs)
    parts = [("_" + p[1:]) if p.startswith(".") else p for p in Path(src).parts]
    return DOCS_DIR.joinpath(*parts).with_name(parts[-1] + ".md")
```

- Maps a source path to its doc path. Any path part starting with `.` gets the dot replaced by `_` (`.claude` becomes `_claude`), so the docs folder is not hidden.
- `Path(src).parts` splits the path into a tuple of names. The list comprehension with `a if cond else b` transforms each one.
- `joinpath(*parts)`: `*` unpacks the list into separate arguments.
- `with_name(parts[-1] + ".md")` replaces the last component with e.g. `code_docs.py.md`. The `.py` stays in the name, so `x.py` and `x.sh` never collide.
- A side effect: a real folder called `_claude` and one called `.claude` would map to the same doc folder. This is unlikely here.

### Lines 49–50: `sha256`

```python
def sha256(path: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
```

- Reads the file as raw bytes and returns the 64-character hex digest. Hashing bytes means the result does not depend on text encoding.

### Lines 53–57: `documented_hash`

```python
def documented_hash(doc: Path) -> str | None:
    if not doc.exists():
        return None
    m = HEADER.search(doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return m.group(2) if m else None
```

- Returns the hash stored in an existing doc, or `None` if the doc does not exist or has no header. `str | None` means "a string or None".
- `HEADER.search` scans the text for the first match. `m.group(2)` is the sha256. `None` never equals a real hash, so a missing or hand-damaged doc counts as stale.

### Lines 61–68: `private_rules`

```python
def private_rules() -> str:
    """The privacy section of private/CONTEXT.md (gitignored, local only), if it exists.
    The agent runs without tools, so it can't read the file itself; its rules go into the prompt."""
    path = PROJECT / "private" / "CONTEXT.md"
    if not path.is_file():
        return ""
    m = re.search(r"^## Privacy section.*?(?=^## |\Z)", path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), flags=re.M | re.S)
    return f"\n\n---\nPRIVATE RULES (local only; follow them, never quote them):\n{m.group(0)}" if m else ""
```

- New function. The docstring gives the reason: `claude -p` runs with `--tools ""`, so the documenter agent cannot open `private/CONTEXT.md`. Whatever it must obey has to be pasted into the prompt.
- `private/` is gitignored, so the file exists only on Roman's machine. If it is missing (for example on a fresh clone), the function returns `""` and the prompt is unchanged.
- The regex starts at a line that begins with `## Privacy section` and matches lazily (`.*?`) up to the next line starting with `## ` or the end of the text (`\A`/`\Z` style anchors: `\Z` is end of string). `re.M` makes `^` match at each line start, `re.S` lets `.` cross newlines. `(?=...)` is a lookahead: it checks what comes next without consuming it.
- If the section is found, the function returns its text under a `PRIVATE RULES` heading that tells the model to follow the rules and never quote them. If the heading is not found, it returns `""`, and the agent runs without those rules and without any warning.
- The content of that section is never written into this repo's files. Only the prompt sent to the model carries it.

### Lines 71–90: `build_prompt`

```python
def build_prompt(src: str, doc: Path) -> str:
    instructions = re.sub(r"\A---.*?---\s*", "", AGENT_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), count=1, flags=re.S)
    instructions += private_rules()
    source = (PROJECT / src).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[:MAX_SOURCE]
    numbered = "\n".join(f"{i:4} | {line}" for i, line in enumerate(source.splitlines(), 1))
    previous = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if doc.exists() else "(none: first version)"
```

- `instructions`: reads the agent file and removes its YAML frontmatter (the `--- ... ---` block at the start). `\A` is the start of the text, `.*?` is a non-greedy match (the shortest one), `re.S` lets `.` match newlines, and `count=1` replaces only the first match. Only the body is sent as the prompt.
- Line 73 (new): `instructions += private_rules()` appends the privacy rules, if any, to the end of the instructions. `+=` on a string builds a new string and rebinds the name.
- `source`: reads the code. `errors="replace"` swaps undecodable bytes for `�` instead of crashing. `[:MAX_SOURCE]` cuts it to 60,000 characters. A longer file is silently truncated, so its doc would miss the end.
- `numbered`: adds line numbers. `enumerate(..., 1)` counts from 1, `{i:4}` pads the number to width 4, and `"\n".join(...)` glues the lines back together. The model uses these numbers for the line ranges in the headings.
- `previous`: the old doc if there is one, so the model can keep wording that is still correct.

```python
    decisions = PROJECT / "DECISIONS.md"
    titles = "\n".join(re.findall(r"^### .+$", decisions.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), flags=re.M)) \
        if decisions.exists() else "(none)"
    index = PROJECT / "learning" / "INDEX.md"
    notes = "\n".join(l for l in index.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if l.startswith("- ")) \
        if index.exists() else "(none)"
```

- `titles`: `re.findall` with `re.M` (so `^` and `$` match at each line) returns every line beginning with `### `, which are the decision titles. The trailing `\` continues the statement on the next line. If the file is missing, the text is `(none)`.
- `notes`: keeps only the lines of `learning/INDEX.md` that start with `- ` (the note entries).
- The model is only given titles and notes, not full contents. That is why the instructions tell it to link only what it was given.

```python
    root = os.path.relpath(PROJECT, doc.parent).replace(os.sep, "/") + "/"
    others = "\n".join(f"- {f} -> {os.path.relpath(doc_path(f), doc.parent)}" for f in code_files() if f != src)
```

- `root`: the relative path from the doc's folder up to the repo root, for example `../../../../`. Links in the doc use it.
- `others`: one line for each other code file with the relative path to its doc, so the model can link between docs. Note that `code_files()` runs `git` again on every call.

```python
    return (f"{instructions}\n\n---\nToday's date: {datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}\n"
            f"File: {src}\nRelative path from the doc to the repo root (<root>): {root}\n\n"
            f"DECISIONS.md titles:\n{titles}\n\nlearning/INDEX.md:\n{notes}\n\n"
            f"Other code files and their docs (relative to this doc):\n{others or '(none)'}\n\n"
            f"---\nPREVIOUS DOC:\n{previous}\n\n---\nSOURCE ({src}):\n{numbered}\n\n"
            "---\nReturn the doc body now, starting with the Summary line.")
```

- Builds the final prompt from adjacent f-strings (Python joins neighbouring string literals). `{datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}` formats the date. `{others or '(none)'}` falls back to `(none)` when the list is empty.
- Order: instructions (plus private rules), date, file name and `<root>`, decision titles, notes, other files, previous doc, numbered source, closing request.

### Lines 93–112: `document`

```python
def document(src: str) -> str:
    doc = doc_path(src)
    digest = sha256(PROJECT / src)
    env = {**os.environ, "DECISION_LOGGER_CHILD": "1"}  # the child session must not trigger hooks again
```

- Documents one file and returns a status string (`ok ...` or `error ...`). It does not raise for a model failure.
- The digest is computed **before** the model call, so the stored hash is the one of the content that was sent. If the file changes during the call, the doc is stale on the next run, as it should be.
- `{**os.environ, ...}` copies the environment and adds one variable. `DECISION_LOGGER_CHILD=1` is the recursion guard (see [Recursion guard via the `DECISION_LOGGER_CHILD` env var](../../../../DECISIONS.md)). The child `claude` session would otherwise fire Stop hooks, which would start this script again.

```python
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:  # run outside the repo so project CLAUDE.md isn't loaded
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["claude", "-p", "--model", "sonnet", "--tools", "",
             "--settings", '{"disableAllHooks": true}', "--no-session-persistence"],
            input=build_prompt(src, doc), capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=tmp, env=env, timeout=400,
        )
```

- A temporary folder is created and deleted at the end of the `with` block. Running there means Claude Code finds no project `CLAUDE.md` to load.
- `claude -p` is headless "print" mode: it reads the prompt, prints the answer, and exits. `--model sonnet` picks the model, `--tools ""` gives it no tools (it only writes text), `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` turns hooks off (a second guard besides the env var), and `--no-session-persistence` does not save the session to disk.
- The prompt goes in through `input=` (standard input). `timeout=400` kills the call after 400 seconds and raises `TimeoutExpired`, which is not caught here (see "What can go wrong").

```python
    out = proc.stdout.strip()
    if proc.returncode != 0 or not out.startswith("Summary:"):
        return f"error {src}: exit {proc.returncode}: {(proc.stderr or out)[:300]!r}"
```

- Validation: the call must exit with 0 **and** the answer must start with `Summary:`. This rejects replies with a preamble, refusals, or error text. On failure it returns an error string with the first 300 characters of stderr (or stdout if stderr is empty). `!r` shows it with quotes and escapes. The old doc stays in place.

```python
    summary, _, body = out.partition("\n")
    doc.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    doc.write_text(
        f"# `{src}`\n\n<!-- generated by .claude/hooks/code_docs.py from {src} (sha256 {digest}) "
        f"on {datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d}; don't edit by hand, it's rewritten when the file changes -->\n\n"
        f"> {summary.removeprefix('Summary:').strip()}\n\n{body.strip()}\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return f"ok {src}"
```

- `partition("\n")` splits at the first newline into the Summary line, the separator (ignored, `_`), and the rest.
- The doc file is assembled as: a title with the file path, the hash comment (what `HEADER` matches), the summary as a Markdown quote (`> ...`), and the model's body. The model's own `Summary:` line is turned into that quote.
- The hash is written only after a successful reply, so a failed run leaves the file stale and it is retried next turn.

### Lines 115–130: `write_index`

```python
def write_index() -> None:
    rows = []
    for doc in sorted(DOCS_DIR.rglob("*.md")):
        if doc.name == "README.md":
            continue
        text = doc.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        m, summary = HEADER.search(text), re.search(r"^> (.+)$", text, flags=re.M)
        if m:
            rows.append(f"| [`{m.group(1)}`]({doc.relative_to(DOCS_DIR).as_posix()}) | "
                        f"{summary.group(1) if summary else ''} |")
```

- Builds one Markdown table row per doc. `rglob("*.md")` finds `.md` files in all subfolders. The index itself (`README.md`) is skipped with `continue`.
- `m` is the header match: group 1 is the source path used as the link text. `summary` is the first line starting with `> `, which is the summary written by `document`.
- A file without the header (not generated by this script) is left out. `doc.relative_to(DOCS_DIR).as_posix()` gives the link target relative to `docs/code/`, with `/` separators.

```python
    (DOCS_DIR / "README.md").write_text(
        "# Code docs\n\nOne doc per code file, ... \n\n| File | What it is |\n|---|---|\n"
        + "\n".join(rows) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
```

- Writes the index: an intro paragraph with links to `DECISIONS.md` and `learning/INDEX.md`, then the table header and the rows. The index is rebuilt completely each time, not edited.

### Lines 133–153: `main`

```python
def main() -> None:
    if (STATE_DIR / "disabled").exists():
        log_run("skip: disabled")
        return
    STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with open(STATE_DIR / "lock", "w") as lock:
        fcntl.flock(lock, fcntl.LOCK_EX)  # overlapping turns wait, then find the work already done
```

- The off switch: if `.claude/code-docs/disabled` exists, log it and stop.
- It opens a lock file and takes an exclusive `flock`. If another copy of the script is running (two turns ending close together), this one waits. When it gets the lock, the first run has already updated the docs, so it finds nothing to do. The lock is released when the file is closed at the end of the `with` block.

```python
        files = code_files()
        stale = [f for f in files if documented_hash(doc_path(f)) != sha256(PROJECT / f)]
        live = {doc_path(f) for f in files}
        removed = [d for d in DOCS_DIR.rglob("*.md") if d.name != "README.md" and d not in live
                   and HEADER.search(d.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))] if DOCS_DIR.exists() else []
        for d in removed:
            d.unlink()
```

- `stale`: files whose stored hash differs from the current one (including docs that do not exist yet).
- `live`: a set of the doc paths that should exist.
- `removed`: generated docs (they have the header) with no matching source file any more, for example after a file was deleted or renamed. A hand-written `.md` without the header is never deleted. If `docs/code` does not exist yet, the list is empty.
- `d.unlink()` deletes the file.

```python
        if not stale and not removed:
            log_run("ok: nothing changed")
            return
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(document, stale))
        write_index()
        log_run("; ".join(results + [f"removed {d.relative_to(DOCS_DIR)}" for d in removed]))
```

- If there is nothing to do, log it and return. This is the common case.
- Otherwise `ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=3)` runs up to 3 `document` calls at the same time. The work is mostly waiting for the `claude` subprocess, so threads are enough. `pool.map` returns the results in input order, and `list(...)` waits for all of them. If `document` raises in one thread, the exception comes out here when `list` reaches that item.
- Then the index is rewritten and one summary line is logged, for example `ok chat.py; error first_call.py: exit 1: '...'; removed old.py.md`.

### Lines 156–160: entry point

```python
if __name__ == "__main__":
    try:
        main()
    except Exception as exc:  # never break the session because of docs
        log_run(f"error: {type(exc).__name__}: {exc}")
```

- `if __name__ == "__main__":` is true only when the file is run directly, not when it is imported.
- `try/except Exception` catches any error from `main`, logs its type and message, and exits normally. A docs failure must never break the Claude session. The traceback is not saved, only the one-line message.

## Trace one run

Situation: Roman edits `chat.py`. The turn ends and the hook calls the script. `first_call.py` and `check_env.py` are unchanged and already documented.

1. `main` finds no `disabled` file, creates `STATE_DIR` if needed, and takes the lock.
2. `code_files()` returns, for example, `['.claude/hooks/code_docs.py', ..., 'chat.py', 'check_env.py', 'first_call.py']`.
3. For each file the stored hash is compared with the current one. Only `chat.py` differs, so `stale = ['chat.py']`. `removed = []`.
4. `document('chat.py')`: `doc = docs/code/chat.py.md`, `digest = '3f9a…'`. `build_prompt` reads the agent instructions, then `private_rules()` appends the privacy section if `private/CONTEXT.md` exists (otherwise it adds `""`). It then adds the date `2026-10-08`, `root = '../../'`, the decision titles, the note lines, the other files, the old doc, and the numbered source (`   1 | import os` and so on).
5. `claude -p` runs in a temp folder and returns text starting with `Summary: Interactive chat loop …`. The return code is 0, so the check passes.
6. The doc is written with a `# \`chat.py\`` title, the hash comment, and `> Interactive chat loop …`.
7. `write_index()` rebuilds `docs/code/README.md`.
8. `runs.log` gets: `2026-10-08T14:05:09 ok chat.py`.

If run again right away, all hashes match and the log says `ok: nothing changed`.

## What can go wrong

- **`claude` returns an error or a reply that doesn't start with `Summary:`:** `document` returns `error chat.py: exit 1: '...'`. This appears only in `runs.log`. The old doc stays and the file is retried on the next run, since its hash is still different.
- **`claude` takes more than 400 s:** `subprocess.run` raises `TimeoutExpired`. `document` does not catch it. It goes up through `pool.map` into `main`, and the top-level handler logs `error: TimeoutExpired: ...`. The effect is larger than one file: `write_index()` and the normal result line are skipped for that run. Docs that other threads already finished are saved.
- **`claude` is not installed or not on `PATH`:** `FileNotFoundError`, handled the same way, logged as `error: FileNotFoundError: ...`.
- **`git` fails** (not a repo, or git is missing): `check=True` raises, and the run logs `error: CalledProcessError: ...` or `FileNotFoundError`.
- **`code-documenter.md` missing:** `AGENT_FILE.read_text` raises `FileNotFoundError` inside `build_prompt`, so every file fails the same way.
- **`private/CONTEXT.md` missing, or no section starting with `## Privacy section`:** `private_rules()` quietly returns `""`. The docs are then generated without those extra rules and nothing is logged. This is the normal case on a clone without the local file, but it also means a renamed heading switches the rules off without any warning.
- **The privacy rules are only an instruction to the model:** nothing in the script checks the finished doc for forbidden content before writing it. The output check is still only "starts with `Summary:`".
- **Files over 60,000 characters:** truncated without warning, so the doc will miss the end of the file. The cap applies to the source only, not to the instructions or the private rules.
- **Wrong or invented content in a doc:** nothing checks the model's output beyond `Summary:` at the start. A wrong line range or a made-up link is written as is.
- **Changed instructions do not refresh old docs:** the hash covers only the source file. Editing `code-documenter.md` or the private file changes no hash, so existing docs are not rewritten until their source changes. To force a refresh, change the source, or delete the doc.
- **Cost:** each stale file is one Sonnet call, so editing many files at once means many calls.
- **Hand-edited docs:** if the header is kept and the source did not change, the edit stays. If the source changes, the doc is rewritten and the edit is lost.
- **Windows:** `fcntl` import fails outside Linux/WSL. This happens at import, before the `try`, so it is not logged.
- **Lock held by a hung run:** other runs wait forever on `flock`, because there is no lock timeout.
- **Failed runs are silent:** the user sees nothing in the session. Check `.claude/code-docs/runs.log`.
